items.title: Marty Grosz interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 4, 1995
items.q: before Trummy Young came on to the scene, I think everybody played [scats].

ctx.x: Well even some of our best horn players that we’ve talked to have mentioned they know the words when they play some of those songs. You need to know the words whether they’re being sung or not.

You need to know, if you’re distorting it, I feel it’s nice to know you’re doing violence to it. It’s nice to know that you’re painting a mustache on Mona Lisa when it’s happening, you know what I mean? Because you can, one of the things that’s often fun that Jimmy Lunceford and Red Nichols used to do was take fast tunes and play them slow, and slow tunes and play them fast. And you know before Trummy Young came on to the scene, I think everybody played [scats]. You know it was one of those kinds of tunes. And…
For our younger viewers, can you tell us what tin pan alley means?
